questions: Should the function assume the DataFrame has exactly two columns named 'X' and 'Y', or should it handle DataFrames with additional columns (ignoring them or raising an error)?
Is the model required to be fitted with X as a DataFrame (single column) and y as a Series, or is it acceptable to use X as a 1D array or Series?
Should the function validate that the numeric values are finite (no NaN or inf) before fitting?
Is the random numeric data guaranteed to be normally distributed, or could it be any numeric distribution (e.g., uniform, integers)?
Should the function return the model object directly, or is it allowed to return additional values (like scores or predictions)?
If the DataFrame has fewer than 100 rows, should the function still work or raise an error?
Is the function expected to handle cases where column 'X' or 'Y' contains non-numeric data (e.g., strings)?
Should the linear regression use default sklearn parameters (fit_intercept=True, etc.), or are custom parameters allowed/required?
